request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the

agent.result_text:
Sheets in the same tree now share one claim-number sequence, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works.** When a claim is opened, its number is the next one after the last number given on any sheet of the tree. The tree means the sheet's topmost parent and every sheet below it. The new number is stored as the opening sheet's own last number. Numbers already given are left as they are. Sheets that number by period still use their own per-period sequence. Two people opening claims at once can't get the same number, because all the tree's sheet rows are locked in id order first.

**What changed** (server only; no schema or front-end change was needed):
- `SheetService.nextClaimNumber` works out the tree and gives the next shared number.
- `SheetRepository` gained two queries: one reads the highest last number across a set of sheets, the other sets a sheet's last number.

**A bug I worked around in existing code:** `PersonTree.othersOf`, which blocks a person name already used elsewhere in the tree, misses sheets below the sheet's own parents. For example, it doesn't search below a sheet that is itself a parent. That's how my first attempt numbered a claim 4 instead of 5. Its own description says it should cover every sheet below the topmost parent, so the name check probably has the same gap. I didn't change it because that's outside this request; the numbering uses its own correct tree lookup. Tell me if you'd like the name check fixed too.

`SheetRepository.advanceClaimNumber` is no longer used; I left it in place.
